title: Zika Virus Disease (ECDC/EU Case Definition)
description: EU/ECDC case definition for Zika virus disease surveillance, per Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2018/945: clinical criteria (rash), laboratory criteria for confirmed and probable cases, and epidemiological criteria (travel/residence in a transmission area or sexual contact with an exposed/confirmed person).
organization: European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control (ECDC)

inclusion_criteria.name: Zika virus disease case classification (probable or confirmed)

values.name: Confirmed case (laboratory criteria for case confirmation)
Detection of Zika virus nucleic acid in a clinical specimen
Detection of Zika virus antigen in a clinical specimen
Isolation of Zika virus from a clinical specimen
Zika-specific IgM antibodies detected, confirmed by neutralisation test
Zika virus specific IgM antibodies detected in serum sample(s)
Seroconversion or four-fold increase in the titre of Zika specific antibodies in paired serum samples
Probable case (clinical, epidemiological and probable-level laboratory criteria)
Travel or residence in transmission area
values.description: History of travel to, or residence in an area with documented on-going transmission of Zika virus, within the two-week period prior to the onset of symptoms

values.name: Sexual contact with exposed or confirmed person
values.description: Sexual contact with a person recently exposed to or confirmed with Zika virus infection

values.name: Zika specific IgM antibodies detected in a serum sample
values.description: Probable-level laboratory criterion (does not require confirmation by neutralisation test)

notes: The EUR-Lex PDF for Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2018/945 is protected by a bot-detection challenge (AWS WAF) and could not be fetched directly; the clinical/laboratory/epidemiological criteria were sourced from ECDC's official case-definition summary page (https://www.ecdc.europa.eu/en/zika-virus-infection/surveillance-and-disease-data/case-definition), which explicitly cites this Decision as its source. Wording is a close paraphrase rather than a verbatim quote of the legal text.
Case classification 'Possible case' is not applicable/defined for this disease in the Decision.

The exact legal wording of the case classification for 'probable' (i.e. whether it strictly requires the combination of clinical + epidemiological + probable-level laboratory criteria, versus clinical + epidemiological alone) could not be independently verified against the primary EUR-Lex text due to the access issue above; this should be re-checked against the primary source before publishing.

references.citation: Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2018/945 of 22 June 2018 on the communicable diseases and related special health issues to be covered by epidemiological surveillance as well as relevant case definitions, Annex II.
European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control (ECDC). Case definition for surveillance of Zika virus infection.

human_readable_definition:
Clinical criteria:
A person presenting with a rash.

Laboratory criteria for confirmed case (at least one of the following):
- Detection of Zika virus nucleic acid in a clinical specimen
- Detection of Zika virus antigen in a clinical specimen
- Isolation of Zika virus from a clinical specimen
- Detection of Zika virus specific IgM antibodies in serum sample(s) AND confirmation by neutralisation test
- Seroconversion or four-fold increase in the titre of Zika specific antibodies in paired serum samples

Laboratory criteria for probable case:
Detection of Zika specific IgM antibodies in a serum sample.

Epidemiological criteria (at least one of the following):
- History of travel to, or residence in an area with documented on-going transmission of Zika virus, within the two-week period prior to the onset of symptoms
- Sexual contact with a person recently exposed to or confirmed with Zika virus infection

Case classification:
A. Possible case: not applicable
B. Probable case: a person meeting the clinical and epidemiological criteria, with a probable-level laboratory result
C. Confirmed case: a person meeting the laboratory criteria for case confirmation
surveillance_system_type: EU epidemiological surveillance under Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2018/945
